name: Canyon_Terrain_Generation
description: The procedural terrain system that generates the canyon shape, depth, width, and erosion features

questions.question: Does the visible terrain generation teach the player about canyon formation processes such as water erosion, uplift, and talus deposition?
Can the terrain generator produce a canyon vista screenshot with dramatic scale that rivals AAA open-world games for marketing use?
Does generated terrain include natural secondary features (alluvial fans, meander scars, slump blocks) that make the canyon feel real and lived-in?
Can canyon terrain be fully generated at editor load time from a seed without requiring manual sculpting or post-processing?
Does terrain generation reuse the existing core/matter_gpu.py heightmap pipeline or does it require a new procedural generation module?
Is the generated canyon terrain compatible with UE5.8 world-partition system for streaming large open-world sections?
Can the terrain LOD system maintain 30+ fps during a fast flythrough of a 4 km canyon section on the target RTX 3060?
Can the terrain scale and camera distance be adjusted for players with simulation-sickness sensitivity to deep canyon drop-offs?
Does canyon shape (width, depth, wall angle, overhangs) propagate realistic acoustic reverb and echo to the audio system?
Does deterministic seed-based terrain generation produce byte-identical heightfield output across all clients?
Can the community generate custom canyon layouts by modifying heightmap seed parameters or supplying custom noise inputs?
Are generated terrain feature names (plateau, butte, arroyo, meander) stored for loc and referenced in educational observations?
Does terrain generation depend on the UE5 landscape subsystem being initialized with procedural material support before generation runs?
Does deterministic seed-based canyon generation prove that the demo can be packaged without prebuilt static level geometry?
Is canyon terrain generation derived from the architectural requirement that all demo environments be procedurally generated?
Does procedural canyon generation conflict with hand-placed demo props such as campsites, survey points, or quest markers?
What knowledge of UE5 procedural mesh generation, PCG volumes, and landscape sculpting APIs is needed to implement this generator?
Does procedural terrain generation serve the seed vision of an infinitely explorable procedurally generated universe?
What is sacrificed by using procedural generation instead of hand-crafted canyon terrain in terms of visual uniqueness and authored storytelling?
How do we know the terrain generator produces geologically plausible canyons rather than aesthetically pleasing noise?
Does the generated terrain physically exist in the UE5 world as Landscape heightfield data that the player can stand on and traverse?
Does terrain generation need sub-features such as biome-specific erosion layers or river-carving simulation, or is a single heightmap generator sufficient?
Are sibling terrain features missing such as cave generation, overhang support, or underground river systems?
Is Demo_Canyon_Terrain detailed enough about procedural generation requirements to fully define the terrain generators scope?
Should terrain generation be built first as the foundation that strata visuals and resource indicators render onto?
Does incomplete terrain generation block all other canyon sub-features making it the hard critical-path dependency?
